title: Postman: requests, variables, environments and collections

videos.script: Every request so far was a line you typed in a terminal. {{terminal}} That works, and it is easy to lose. Type it again tomorrow and one header goes missing. This lesson moves the requests into Postman, a desktop app built to keep them. {{postman}} You send a first request and read the answer in panes. The status, the time and the size sit on one line. The headers and the body sit underneath. {{panes}} Then the address stops being written out. It becomes a variable called baseUrl, and an environment says what it holds. {{variables}} Switch the environment and the same requests talk to another server. A variable can be defined in five places. When two of them disagree, one rule decides which wins. {{scopes}} Last, the requests go into a collection. Folders group them, and the token is set once for all of them. {{collection}} You keep that collection as a file of your own, not only inside the app. Lesson 5 adds tests to it. Lesson 6 runs it with no window at all. {{file}}
